text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Renault remains firm on Vilvoorde plant shutdown despite attacks from politicians and trade union leaders. The carmaker will lay off an additional 2,764 employees in France.

-- European Commissioner Karel van Miert says Renault seems to have violated two E.U. directives but recommends legal action through Belgian and French national courts. Says European Commission powerless to act.
-- Coca Cola KOF1.MX appeals French ruling on dominant market position.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Political leaders and trade unions in Belgium and France lash out against Renault's brutal attitude.
-- Paris court orders Societe Generale to pay Credit Lyonnais one franc in damages and 50,000 francs in legal fees for unfair marketing practices.
-- Algeria and European Union open talks in Brussels on free trade area.
-- Alcatel Alsthom ex-chairman Pierre Suard pleads not guilty to misappropriating corporate funds.
-- Dassault and Aerospatiale to seek Bourse listing after privatisation.

-- Bertelsmann's board member Michael Dornemann says in interview increasing stake in Premiere attractive from economic point of view. If Canal Plus and Kirch want to resolve their differences Bertelsmann ready to talk with them.
L'AGEFI
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis wants pubic enquiry into GAN losses which will require 20 billion franc bailout from the government.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Thomson-CSF source says net profit should be 700 to 800 million francs while independent analysts predict up to 1.2 billion.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- One-day civil servant strike set for tomorrow.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- General Motors said Tuesday that job cuts at Renault and Ford signaled the start of a long-awaited shakeout in the European auto industry.
